lines: ### ISSUE-1655: Every streamed message update reads and transacts on the shared session doc (core/store/slices/agent/agentSess [O2]
+- **Status:** 🟡 PARTIAL — change on branch `claude/session-stream-writes`; not yet seen on production
- **Fix:** See plan phase table for the owning phase.
- **Acceptance:** Failing-first regression test, then fix; real signed-in acceptance stays PARTIAL per `.agent/REAL_USER_AUTHENTICITY.md`.

+- **Change (2026-11-23):** text streaming was already coalesced into one write lane per message (`enqueueStreamingText`), but each write still did a `getDocFromServer` on the session plus a transaction that wrote `updatedAt`/`messageStorage` to the shared session doc, so parallel seats' transactions conflicted. `SessionService.updateMessage` now reads the generation inside the transaction and writes only the message doc (the separate server read stays only for attachment uploads). Rules unaffected (`getAfter` on the session works without a session write). Tests: new streaming case (no server read, one write, message doc only) fails on the old code; attachment test now asserts no session write; session + agent store suites 9 files passed; ESLint 0 errors; renderer tsc 0 errors. Not measured live: retry counts with several seats.
### ISSUE-1656: The 300s overall timeout (AS:514, :582-588) overwrites the Conductor's finished reply (seat 0 reuses responseI [O3]
### ISSUE-1658: Per-seat pre-flight is ~6 serial uncached round trips [O5]
+- **Status:** 🟡 PARTIAL — capability snapshot part changed on branch `claude/seat-preflight`; trace, budget and reservation round trips unchanged
- **Fix:** See plan phase table for the owning phase.
- **Acceptance:** Failing-first regression test, then fix; real signed-in acceptance stays PARTIAL per `.agent/REAL_USER_AUTHENTICITY.md`.

+- **Change (2026-11-23, part 1 of O5):** `loadCapabilitySnapshot` fetched the `getCapabilitySnapshot` callable for every seat (20 s timeout each). It now reuses a fresh server snapshot until the snapshot's own `expiresAt` (per signed-in uid), shares one in-flight request between parallel seats, and never caches a fail-closed result. Tests: `CapabilitySnapshotService.cache.test.ts` (3 parallel seats → 1 request; refetch after expiry; failure not cached); agent suites passed; renderer tsc 0 errors; ESLint 0 errors. Not changed: awaited `startTrace`, per-loop `checkBudget`, and the serial quota → headers → reservation calls.
### ISSUE-1659: Persona finalizer adds 2 LLM calls per seat inside the chunk barrier (AS:1634, PersonaResponseService.ts:171-1 [O6]
+- **Status:** 🟡 PARTIAL — change on branch `claude/persona-finalizer`; not yet seen on production
- **Fix:** See plan phase table for the owning phase.
- **Acceptance:** Failing-first regression test, then fix; real signed-in acceptance stays PARTIAL per `.agent/REAL_USER_AUTHENTICITY.md`.

+- **Change (2026-11-23):** in the Boardroom seat loop the persona style pass (`applyCompletedResponse` → `finalizePersonaAgentResponse`, 2 model calls) was awaited inside the chunk, so the next chunk's seats waited for it. The seat's own reply is now shown at once (not streaming) and passed to later seats as context; the style pass runs in the background and replaces the text when ready (a failure keeps the reply as shown). Direct and department flows are unchanged. Test: a style pass that never finishes no longer blocks chunk 2 (on the old code `executeFlow` would hang); boardroom intent suite 31/31; agent + persona suites passed; renderer tsc 0 errors; ESLint 0 errors. Trade-off: a styled reply may replace the plain one a few seconds after it appears.
### ISSUE-1660: Action steps never stream tokens and drop agent prose from receipts (AS:1360-1386, BoardroomActionPlan.ts:206) [O7]
### ISSUE-1661: History summarization blocks every send but agents discard it (HistoryManager.ts:105-118, BaseAgent.ts:1120-11 [O8]
+- **Status:** 🟡 PARTIAL — change on branch `claude/history-summary-unused`; not yet seen on production
- **Fix:** See plan phase table for the owning phase.
- **Acceptance:** Failing-first regression test, then fix; real signed-in acceptance stays PARTIAL per `.agent/REAL_USER_AUTHENTICITY.md`.

+- **Change (2026-11-23):** reproduced on production as part of ISSUE-1710 ("Timed out during older conversation summary" at 5 s and "Failed to generate a complete history summary" on every send in a 2,305-turn session). `HistoryManager.summarizeOlder` now folds whole turns and saves progress after each one; the send waits at most 5 s as before, but the summary is no longer cancelled and keeps running in the background, so a later send reuses it; a send that can't wait uses the part that is done, with a note on how much it covers (Jev on that model-facing note: 1 call, 529/69 tokens, 0/1 flagged). `BaseAgent` now puts the older-turn summary in front of the structured recent turns (`withOlderHistorySummary`), so agents receive it. The "saved memories unavailable" reply warning now appears only when memories were actually unavailable. Tests: long-session background case + helper tests; two bound tests now expect 4 calls (the oversized turn is folded on its own); agent suites 267 files passed; typecheck exit 0; ESLint 0 errors.
### ISSUE-1662: Trivial "hi" runs the full paid swarm; Boardroom instant greeting is dead (AS:1232, AS:349-354, AS:838) [O9]
### ISSUE-1693: Dropping an audio file anywhere in the web app always fails ("Failed to save to cloud library")
+- **Status:** 🟡 PARTIAL — data-URL upload changed in #1002; simulated progress replaced on branch `claude/dropzone-real-progress`; not yet seen on production
- **Module:** Global drop zone / StorageService / Hosting CSP

- **Evidence:** production build `8253704d3`, 2026-11-22 ~01:30 UTC, owner account, built-in browser. Dragging `Assembly Line Halo.wav` (WAV, 16-bit/48 kHz, 33.5 MB) onto the page while the Publishing Create Release dialog was open put two entries in the Upload Queue, both "Failed to save to cloud library"; a dropped PNG in the same gesture succeeded. Console: `Connecting to 'data:audio/wav;base64,…' violates the following Content Security Policy directive: "connect-src 'self' blob: …"`, then `[StorageService] Cloud upload failed: TypeError: Failed to fetch` and `[Store] Failed to save item`. Source: `GlobalDropZone.tsx` reads the file with `FileReader` into a `data:` URL (`:169-189`) and calls `addUploadedAudio`; `StorageService` uploads audio/video data URLs with `await (await fetch(item.url)).blob()` (`packages/renderer/src/services/StorageService.ts:225`). `firebase.json`'s CSP `connect-src` has `'self' blob:` but no `data:`, so that fetch is always refused on hosted web. Images take a different branch and succeed.

- **Fix:** convert the dropped `File` straight to a `Blob` (no `data:` round trip) and upload with `uploadBytes`; or decode the base64 without `fetch` as the image branch does. Do not widen the CSP to `data:`. Replace the simulated progress with real `uploadBytesResumable` progress. Consider letting an open dialog with a file input claim the drop.

- **Acceptance:** on https://indii.music with a genuine account, drop a real WAV: it appears in the library, survives reload and plays; progress reflects bytes sent; no CSP error in the console. Unit test covers the audio branch without `fetch(data:)`.

+- **Change (2026-11-23):** the CSP cause was addressed in #1002 (`mediaUrlToBlob` decodes `data:` URLs locally instead of `fetch`). Branch `claude/dropzone-real-progress` removes the simulated progress (random delay and random increments) from `GlobalDropZone`: the item is marked uploading at once and progress is the `FileReader` read progress. Test `GlobalDropZone.test.tsx` (drop a file → progress ends at 100, then success); it would also pass on the old code, so it guards the flow rather than proving the change. ESLint 0 errors. Still open: the base64 round trip holds a 33 MB WAV as a ~45 MB string, and a drop over an open dialog goes to the global queue.
### ISSUE-1694: A master ingested on the web never reaches the track library, so Submit Release cannot list it
+- **Status:** 🟡 PARTIAL — change on branch `claude/qc-master-to-library`; not yet seen on production
- **Module:** Distribution QC (Pre-Flight Audio & QC) / Track library / Submit Release

- **Evidence:** source on main `8253704d3`. Submit Release lists only masters from `trackLibrary.list()` (`users/{uid}/tracks` with `masterFingerprint` and `masterAsset.audioProperties`; `SubmitReleaseModal.tsx:118-121`), and the live account showed "No canonical masters found — ingest one first" (2026-11-21 run). Distribution's own ingest, the QC tab's web path, uploads the master (`masterAudioService.persist`) and waits for the server analysis receipt (`QCPanel.tsx:233-251`), but never calls `trackLibrary.saveTrack`; no Cloud Function writes `users/{uid}/tracks` from that receipt (only the developer SDK endpoint `sdkTracks.ts:35` creates tracks). On the web, the only UI that saves a canonical master to the library is the Creative video storyboard's audio upload (`StoryboardTimeline.tsx:196`, via `trackIngestion.ingestTrack`).

- **Fix:** after a successful canonical-master analysis on the web, save the track to the library through the same `trackIngestion` path the storyboard uses (one ingestion service, not a second copy), or point Submit Release's empty state at a path that does.
- **Acceptance:** on production with a genuine account, ingest a WAV in Distribution → Pre-Flight Audio & QC, open Submit Release, and select that master; reload keeps it.

+- **Change (branch `claude/qc-master-to-library`, 2026-11-23):** `TrackIngestionService.saveAnalyzedMaster` (steps 4-5 of ingestion, extracted so there is one path) maps an already uploaded and analysed master to library metadata and saves it; `ingestTrack` now calls it, and the QC panel's web path calls it after the analysis receipt. A failed library write no longer hides the analysis: it shows "Your master was analyzed, but it could not be added to your track library. Try again before submitting a release." (Jev: 1 call, 500/71 tokens, 0/1 flagged). Test: `saveAnalyzedMaster` saves without re-uploading or re-analysing; ingestion + distribution suites 17 files passed; typecheck exit 0; ESLint 0 errors. Not verified live.
### ISSUE-1695: Publishing catalogue fails with "Missing or insufficient permissions" in the personal workspace
- **Status:** 🟡 PARTIAL — repair on branch `claude/publishing-personal-workspace` (with ISSUE-1696); awaiting deploy and a genuine production check

- **Production check after #1008 (2026-11-23 14:07 UTC, build `925d01f53`, deploy run actions/runs/45186524129, owner's existing session, no mocks):** the send still failed, now with the plain text "Getting this reply ready took too long. Please send your message again." The new stage log names the cause: `{"context store":207,"working context":208,"conversation history":6260,"memory recall":17339,"active plans":17339,"product skill":17339,"elapsedMs":30059}` — the directive read started at 0.2 s and was still pending at 30 s. Every Firestore read in the turn hit its limit (saved memories 1 s, older summary 5 s, plans 3 s, memory recall 8 s, fallback 3 s); the REST aggregation calls on load finished in under 250 ms. IndexedDB showed 5 app tabs sharing the Firestore cache (`persistentMultipleTabManager`, `experimentalForceLongPolling`), with the network owner a background tab (`inForeground: false`); reads from other tabs go through it. Likely cause: the owner tab is throttled by Chrome. Not proven (no single-tab run yet).

- **Third fix (branch `claude/firestore-read-stall`):** `ArtistDirectiveService.getDirective` waits 5 s for the server, then uses the copy saved on this device if there is one (not kept in memory, so the next turn asks the server again); with no saved copy it keeps waiting for the server as before. Tests: 3 new cases (device copy after 5 s then server next time; no device copy waits for server; fast server never reads the device copy); renderer services 641 files passed, only the 2 known `milestones.test.ts` failures; typecheck exit 0; ESLint 0 errors. Not verified: whether this device's cache holds the directive, and the multi-tab cause itself (next: a run with only one app tab open, and a decision on the tab manager).

+- **Fourth fix (branch `claude/firestore-tab-cache`, owner approved changing tab behaviour 2026-11-23):** Firestore now uses `persistentSingleTabManager({ forceOwnership: false })` instead of the shared multi-tab cache. The first app tab keeps the offline cache; any other tab falls back to an in-memory cache with its own connection (the SDK does this on `failed-precondition`), so a throttled background tab can no longer hold up reads in the visible one. Trade-off: extra tabs lose offline persistence across reloads and no longer share cached data. Production repeat on build `057eba5c2` (with #1010, 2026-11-23 17:07 UTC): same timeout; stage log `{"conversation history":5236,"memory recall":16314,…,"elapsedMs":30030}` with the directive still pending at 30 s, so the device-copy fallback did not help in shared-cache mode. content.thinking:
I'm working out why the prompt shows on every load. My guess is the cloud snapshot comes from another device, since the user has a desktop, a web app, and several browsers. Once they cancel, the local state should push to the cloud, so the next load ought to match this device and skip the prompt, unless the push is blocked or the device ID isn't persisting.

I'm considering whether the other device keeps pushing newer state, so each load finds a newer snapshot and prompts. If that's the case, the prompt is reasonable. A better fix is to skip it when the local workspace has nothing in it, since there's no unsaved work to protect. In that situation I'd load the cloud snapshot directly, which also avoids the risk of overwriting the cloud with an empty state. I still need to find out how to check whether the local workspace is empty, which means looking at what `workspaceSyncService` exposes for building a snapshot.

The sync prompt shows up whenever another device saved the workspace more recently, even though this device almost never has unsaved work on a fresh load. I'm changing it to load the cloud copy silently when the local workspace is empty, and checking the sync API next.

Two more PRs are up: ISSUE-1712 (dialog under the side panel) and the 1708(a) workspace prompt. Neither is deployed yet.

- **[#1025](https://github.com/indii-music-founder/indii-music-founder/pull/1025) (ISSUE-1712):** the Create Release dialog now centres in the space beside the side panel instead of under it. The panel stays clickable, which the cover pick from Project Assets needs. I applied the same layout to the live page and reverted it afterwards. Next was covered before and clickable after, with the dialog ending at x=896 and the panel starting at x=1120.
- **[#1026](https://github.com/indii-music-founder/indii-music-founder/pull/1026) (ISSUE-1708a):** the "newer workspace" prompt was showing on every page load. Now, if this device has no notes, referenced assets, plan or typed prompt that the cloud copy lacks, the newer copy loads without asking. If it does, the prompt appears as before. This loads the cloud copy rather than keeping an empty one, so it can't overwrite the cloud with an empty workspace, which is why the earlier attempt was reverted.

The new tests pass, along with the publishing and hooks suites, and typecheck and ESLint are clean.
